title: Plasma Treatment Strategies for Tailoring the Thickness and Surface Chemistry of VSe2 and V2O5 for Magnetic Material Design
content: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) materials have garnered significant attention due to their unique electronic, magnetic, and optical properties, making them promising candidates for applications in next generation nanoelectronics, quantum computing, and energy storage devices [1, 2]. These materials are typically fabricated using methods such as mechanical exfoliation, chemical vapor deposition (CVD), or molecular beam epitaxy (MBE). However, certain post-processing techniques, such as plasma treatment, can be essential for modifying their structural and electronic properties, which are essential for the development of more efficient electronic and optoelectronic devices. Specifically, these post-processing steps could play a key role in advancing quantum devices [1].
